title: Precision fingerprint ingestion and canary sampling for low-precision model variants
creator: Sophie Chen
description:
Problem: When we onboard low-precision variants (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8) we frequently see subtle quality regressions that only show up on specific prompt families or at scale (tail latency and token-level hallucination increases). Current onboarding relies on bulk metric comparisons and ad-hoc speech tests; there is no compact artifact that uniquely identifies workload sensitivity for a model variant.

Goal: Build a small, portable 'precision fingerprint' artifact produced at quant-profile creation time that captures (1) prompt sensitivity signals across a curated golden prompt set, (2) distributional token-level divergence sketches, and (3) latency/cost microbenchmarks. Use this fingerprint to drive a canary sampling policy: route a configurable fraction of production traffic that matches fingerprint clusters to the candidate variant and run statistical delta detectors. Establish automated gating criteria for rollout, rollback, and pinning.

Scope:
- Define fingerprint schema (string lists only in ticket: features: prompt_family_scores, token_divergence_histogram_buckets, tail_latency_percentiles, per-route acceptance thresholds).
- Implement fingerprint extractor in the quant-profile compilation pipeline so artifacts are written to the variant registry.
- Extend runtime router to support fingerprint-aware sampling keys and deterministic hashing for reproducible canary cohorts.
- Add an automated delta-detector job that consumes canary vs baseline streams and emits alerts when predefined thresholds are crossed (statistical test: two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov for divergence + bootstrap CI for difference in mean reward).
- Publish console widgets for fingerprint comparison and canary health (delta values, p-values, sample sizes, and suggested actions).

Acceptance criteria:
- Fingerprint artifact produced in quant-profile release flow and attached to variant metadata.
- Canary sampler can be configured per-customer/per-route with sample allocation and fingerprint-match rules.
- Automated detector produces alerts with clear operator guidance and links to failing prompt examples.
- Rollout policy can automatically pause or rollback a variant when regression criteria are met.

Non-goals: end-to-end model retraining, retraining pipelines, or replacing full eval harnesses. This focuses on short, targeted detection for early-stage regressions during rollout.
